titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Abraham, Melchizedek and the Blind Jew (ch. 105)
part: ch. 105 — Abraham, Melchizedek and the Blind Jew
about: The author, arguing against a Jewish reader, says that Abraham and the prophets were justified by faith in the coming of Christ. In a reported dialogue God sends Abraham to Melchizedek at Salem, where bread and wine prefigure the Eucharist; the chapter ends by rebuking the blind Jew with Isaiah's words.

sentences.i: Chapter 105: Concerning the Faith of Abraham
sentences.n: Chapter heading. አሚነ is the accusative of አሚን 'faith' (from አምነ 'believe'); the heading is 'concerning Abraham's faith', with አብርሃም in construct-like sequence after it. በእንተ takes what follows as its object, as in the pilot.

sentences.t: ወአንተሰ ፡ ኢትሌቡ ፡ ከመ ፡ በአሚን ፡ ይጸድቁ ፡ ከመ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ወዳዊት ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ በበ ፡ መትልው ፡ እለ ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ለወልደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: And-as-for-you not-you-understand that by-faith they-are-justified, like Abraham and-David and-all-of-them prophets, each-in succession(?), who they-prophesied concerning his-coming of-the-son-of God.
sentences.i: And you — do you not understand that they are made righteous by faith, as Abraham and David and all the prophets were, each in his own turn, who prophesied about the coming of the Son of God?
sentences.n: ወአንተሰ: ወ- 'and' + አንተ 'you (ms)' + emphatic -ሰ 'as for'. ኢትሌቡ (?) is read as a 2nd-person plural negative of ለበወ 'understand' (an irregular spelling for ኢትለብዉ), so a question 'do you not understand'; the singular አንተ with a plural verb is odd and the form is uncertain. ይጸድቁ is 3mp subjunctive of ጸድቀ 'be righteous, justified' after ከመ. በበ መትልው (?): distributive በበ 'each' + መትልው, which I take as 'succession, one following another' ('each in his turn'); this is a guess. እለ ተነበዩ 'who prophesied' (ተነበየ, tä-stem of n-b-y). ለወልደ እግዚኣብሔር: ለ- marks the genitive/object, construct 'son-of'. Here the writer, arguing against a Jewish interlocutor, claims the patriarchs were justified by faith in the coming Christ.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ በመዋዕልየኑ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ትፌኑ ፡ ቃልከ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ምድር ፤
sentences.l: And-said Abraham, 'In-my-days-indeed(?), O-Lord, wilt-thou-send(?) thy-word upon earth?'
sentences.i: And Abraham said, 'O Lord, in my days will you send your word upon the earth?'
sentences.n: The speaker shifts here: from the author addressing the Jew to a reported dialogue between Abraham and God. በመዋዕልየኑ: በ- 'in' + መዋዕል 'days' + -የ 'my' + -ኑ, the interrogative enclitic (?), so a question. ትፌኑ (?) read as 2ms imperfect of ፌነወ 'send'; it could also be a statement 'you will send'. ቃልከ 'your word' is the Word of God, i.e. Christ, in the author's reading. The exchange is not from Genesis; it is the author's own expansion.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አልቦ ፡ ኢበጽሐ ፡ ጊዜሁ ፡ አላ ፡ ኣርእየከ ፡ አምሳለ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ወባሕቱ ፡ ዕዲ ፡ ዮርዳኖስ ፡ ወተጠመቅ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ተዐዲ ፡ ወብጻሕ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሳሌም ፡ ወትረክቦ ፡ ለመልከ ፡ ጼዴቅ ፡ ወአነ ፡ እኤዝዞ ፡ ያርኢከ ፡ ተኣምሪሁ ፡ ወአምሳሊሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-said-to-him God, 'No; not-has-arrived his-time, but I-will-show-you likeness-of his-coming. And-but cross Jordan and-be-baptized while you-cross(?) and-arrive (at) city-of Salem and-you-will-find Melchizedek, and-I I-will-command-him that-he-show-you his-wonders and-his-likenesses.'
sentences.i: And God said to him, 'No; his time has not yet come, but I will show you a likeness of his coming. Cross the Jordan and be baptized as you cross, and come to the city of Salem, and you will find Melchizedek; and I will command him to show you his wonders and his likenesses.'
sentences.n: God answers; the speaker is God, the addressee Abraham (ወይቤሎ 'and he said to him', ብህለ + -ሎ). አልቦ 'there is not' as a reply 'no'. ኢበጽሐ 'has not arrived' (3ms perfect). ኣርእየከ is read as 1cs imperfect of አርአየ 'show' with the long initial vowel, 'I will show you' (?). ዕዲ is an imperative of ዐደወ 'cross' (?); ተዐዲ after እንዘ 'while' as 2ms imperfect 'while you cross' (?), though it may be a repeated imperative; ተጠመቅ 'be baptized' (tä-stem imperative); ብጻሕ imperative 'arrive', its object ሀገረ ሳሌም in the accusative/construct. The baptism of Abraham is the author's own motif. ትረክቦ 2ms imperfect 'you will find him'; እኤዝዞ 1cs 'I will command him'; ያርኢከ 3ms subjunctive 'that he show you'. Genesis 14:18 names Melchizedek king of Salem; ለመልከ ጼዴቅ is written as two words in the edition, with ለ- marking the object.

sentences.t: ወገብረ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ወረከቦ ፡ ለመልከ ፡ ጼዴቅ ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ምሥጢረ ፡ ኅብስት ፡ ወወይን ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዘተገብረ ፡ በፋሲካነ ፡ ለመድኀኒትነ ፡ በእግዚእነ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ዝኬ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ተምኔቱ ፡ ወትፍሥሕቱ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ ዐዊዶ ፡ ምሥዋዐ ፡ ዘገብረ ፡ መልከ ፡ ጼዴቅ ፡ ነሢኦ ፡ ጸበርተ ፡ ወበቀልተ ፡ በዕለተ ፡ ሰንበት ፤
sentences.l: And-he-did likewise and-found Melchizedek, and-gave-him mystery-of bread and-wine, that-which was-done at-our-Passover for-our-savior, in-our-Lord Jesus Christ. This(?) he (was) his-desire and-his-joy, of-Abraham, having-circled(?) altar which made Melchizedek, having-taken [ጸበርተ (?)] and-herbs(?) on-day-of Sabbath;
sentences.i: And he did so, and found Melchizedek, and Melchizedek gave him the mystery of bread and wine — that which was done at our Passover for our Savior, in our Lord Jesus Christ. This was Abraham's desire and joy, as he went about the altar that Melchizedek had made, taking up a loaf(?) and herbs(?) on the day of the Sabbath;
sentences.n: Genesis 14:18 (Melchizedek brings out bread and wine) is read as a type of the Eucharist; ምሥጢር 'mystery' also means 'sacrament', and Passover (ፋሲካ) is the Christian Pascha. ውእቱ ዘተገብረ 'that which was done' (ዘ- relative + passive ተገብረ). ዝኬ (?) taken as the demonstrative ዝ + enclitic -ኬ, 'this indeed'; ውእቱ is the copula. ተምኔቱ 'his desire' (ተምኔት + -ሁ) and ትፍሥሕቱ 'his joy', with ለአብርሃም marking the owner. ዐዊዶ (?) is read as a converb 'having encircled, gone around' (ዐወደ), but the form and the sense are doubtful; ምሥዋዐ accusative 'altar'. ነሢኦ 'having taken' (converb of ነሥአ). ጸበርተ (?) I cannot place; I suggest a kind of bread or cake and mark it uncertain; ወበቀልተ (?) is read as ወ- + በቀልት 'herbs, vegetables' (accusative). The Sabbath detail is the author's own; the clause ends with ፤ though the sentence continues.

sentences.t: በተአምኖኬ ፡ ከመ ፡ ተፈሥሐ ፡ ርኢ ፡ ወበተአምኖ ፡ ጸድቀ ፡ ርኢ ፤
sentences.l: By-his-faith-indeed(?) how he-rejoiced, see; and-by-faith he-was-justified(?), see;
sentences.i: Through his faith — see how he rejoiced; and through faith — see — he was made righteous;
sentences.n: The author turns to the reader. ርኢ is a 2ms imperative of ርእየ 'see', here a rhetorical 'look!'. በተአምኖኬ: በ- 'by' + ተአምኖ 'faith, confession' (from አምነ) + -ኬ; the pronoun is unmarked, so 'his' is inferred (?). ጸድቀ ርኢ is uncertain: either 'see, he was justified' (perfect) or 'see righteousness' (accusative noun). The pairing echoes the justification of Abraham by faith (Genesis 15:6) without quoting it.

sentences.t: ኦአይሁዳዊ ፡ ዕዉር ፡ እንዘ ፡ ብከ ፡ አዕይንተ ፡ ኢትሬኢ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ብከ ፡ እዝ ፡ ነ ፡ ኢትሰምዕ ፤
sentences.l: O-Jew, blind one, while to-you eyes you-do-not-see, and-while to-you ears [እዝ ነ (?)] you-do-not-hear;
sentences.i: O Jew, blind man, though you have eyes you do not see, and though you have ears you do not hear;
sentences.n: ኦአይሁዳዊ (?) is written as one word: ኦ 'O' (vocative particle) + አይሁዳዊ 'Jew'. ዕዉር 'blind'. ብከ 'you have' (ቦ + -ከ, the existential way of saying 'have'). እዝ ነ is two words in the edition; I read it as a split of እዝነ 'ears' (accusative plural/ear of; a split ear? uncertain), since the parallel with አዕይንተ 'eyes' calls for it. Not the suffix -ነ 'our' as in the glossary entry elsewhere. ኢትሬኢ 'you do not see' and ኢትሰምዕ 'you do not hear' are 2ms imperfect negatives; the Jew is addressed in the singular.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ በእንቲአክሙ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ዖሩ ፡ አዕይንቲሆሙ ፡ ወተጸለለ ፡ ልቦሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይለብዉ ፡ ወኢይሣህሎሙ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: As said concerning-you Isaiah prophet, 'They-were-blind(?) their-eyes and-was-darkened their-heart, that-not they-understand and-not he-have-mercy-on-them(?)'
sentences.i: As Isaiah the prophet said about you: 'Their eyes were blinded and their hearts were darkened, so that they should not understand and not be pitied.'
sentences.n: Allusion to Isaiah 6:10 (the hardening of the heart; in Geʿez numbering also ኢሳይያስ 6:10), as the author remembers and applies it, not a verbatim quotation. በእንቲአክሙ 'concerning you (plural)' (በእንተ + -ክሙ). ዖሩ (?) may be a contracted 3mp perfect of ዐወረ 'be blind' ('they were blinded'); the reading is uncertain. ተጸለለ 'was overshadowed, darkened' (tä-stem). ከመ ኢይለብዉ 'that they not understand' (3mp subjunctive, as with ኢትሌቡ above; the spelling here is regular). ወኢይሣህሎሙ (?): ይሣህሎሙ read as a 3ms subjunctive 'he pity them' with -ሎሙ 'to them', 'and that He not have mercy on them'; the verb form is uncertain. The part ends with the run of ፨ marks, closing the chapter.
